title: The value of education, training and experience to improve the accuracy of identification: a commentary on ‘Inter- and intra-observer variation in phytolith morphometry’
content: Confidence in the correct identification of an object at the macroscopic and microscopic level is critical across the biological sciences including the fields of medicine, forensic anthropology, archaeology, ornithology, ecology, botany, visual arts and citizen science. Replicability of identifications within these disciplines is essential for cross-sectional studies and diagnostic tests. A new paper by the members of the International Committee for Phytolith Morphometrics (ICPM) in this issue of Annals of Botany examines factors determining the ability to correctly identify phytoliths (a type of microscopic plant remain) by the same scholar (intra-variability) and between different scholars (inter-variability) (Out et al., 2024). The results are a positive step towards increasing the reliability of phytolith identification in botanical, palaeobotanical, palaeoecological and archaeobotanical research and point towards a surprisingly simple solution: increased education and training.
